fields.aka: Narahari Cakravartī, Ghanaśyāma Cakravartī, Ghanaśyāma dāsa, Narahari dāsa, Narahari Dāsa Ghanaśyāma Dāsa, Rasuiyā Pūjārī, Narahari Cakravartī (Ghanaśyāma)
fields.notes:
Son of Jagannātha, a disciple of Viśvanātha Cakravartī; born at Reñāpur (Reñāgrām), Murshidabad (the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna: at the beginning of the 17th century). Unmarried until his parents died; then by Govindajī's order His cook in Vṛndāvana («Rasuiyā Pūjārī»). Cook, singer, musician and great devotee; wrote the lives of the ācāryas after Mahāprabhu (Bhakti-ratnākara, Narottama-vilāsa); the fifth and twelfth waves of the Bhakti-ratnākara map Vraja and Navadvīpa.

He had two names: Ghanaśyāma (also his signature in his songs) and Narahari — «Narahari dāsa Ghanaśyāma dāsa»; Ghanaśyāma Cakravartī #328 was the same person (merged 06-11-2026, Whisper). Not Ghanaśyāma Cakravartī of Budhuri, grandson of Govinda Kavirāja.

Original Work: Aṣṭakālīya-līlā-smaraṇa-maṅgala-stotram (Sanskrit)

Original Author: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī

Vrajabhāṣā Translator: Ghanaśyāma Dāsa (Narahari Cakravartī Ṭhākura)

Nature of the Work: Poetic verse translation (padānuvāda) adapting Rūpa Gosvāmī's framework of the eight-fold daily pastimes (aṣṭa-kālīya-līlā) of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa into Vrajabhāṣā metrics for devotional singing (kīrtana) and meditation (smaraṇa).

 The record «Narahari Cakravartī (Ghanaśyāma)» #976, which had nothing but the name, was joined to this one (07-11-2026).

fields.aka: Śrīnātha Ācārya, Śrīnātha Cakravartī, Śrīnātha Paṇḍita
fields.notes: Also called Śrīnātha Paṇḍita. The record «Śrīnātha Paṇḍita» #1955, which had nothing but the name, was joined to this one (07-11-2026).

Kālidāsa was born as Malli, the daughter of Pulinda (past life). In his current life he lived in Sankhanagar, Saptagrama. He is described as an uncle of Raghunātha dāsa.

Known as «Bhakta Kālidāsa». The record «Bhakta Kālidās» #117, which had nothing but the name, was joined to this one (07-11-2026).
